transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, to tell you the truth, it’s my wife who really wanted me to come talk to you. I feel fine, I've got plenty of energy, but... well, I guess what brings me in is this memorial I'm putting together for my brother. I started out just wanting to do something nice, you know, a proper tribute, but it’s... it’s gotten a whole lot bigger than I originally meant it to. I just keep getting all these incredible ideas for it, and I have to follow through on them. 

I’ve been spending most days, I mean right from the crack of dawn, just chasing down specific songs he used to listen to back in the seventies. I’m on the phone constantly, calling folks we grew up with, tracking down old friends we haven't spoken to in forty years. I'm planning out these big, elaborate displays with his photos and keepsakes, and I'm even putting together an itinerary for some trips out of state to collect more of his things from people who knew him. There's just so much to coordinate, you know? You have to get these things exactly right. 

But my wife... she’s getting really frustrated with me. She says I’ve completely pushed aside the garden, and usually I'm out there every single day this time of year tending to the tomatoes, but I just haven't had a spare minute for it. I haven't been going to my morning walking group with the guys, either. She says I’ve pushed aside just about everything else in my life for this memorial. I just... I don't think she understands how important it is that I get this all done, and there is just so much ground to cover.
Have you noticed any change in how much sleep you need lately?

Sleep? Well, you know, it's funny you bring that up because my wife was just saying something about that the other day. She was complaining that I'm up at all hours, but honestly, I haven't really noticed a difference in how much I *need*. I mean, I'm just so busy with the memorial, you know? 

Like I was saying, there's just so much to do. I'll be laying in bed, and suddenly I'll remember a song we used to listen to in his old Chevy Nova—it was this beautiful cherry red, you don't see cars like that anymore—and I just have to get up and write it down or try to find it right then and there. If I don't, I might lose the thought, and it has to be perfect. So, I might be up a bit more, pacing around the living room, making lists, organizing his old baseball cards... I found this whole box of them in the attic, and I'm trying to figure out how to display them. Should they go chronologically? Or maybe by team? It's a lot to think about. 

But as for actually needing less sleep? I don't know, I feel fine. I've got all this energy to keep going. I'm not dragging my feet or anything. I just get up when the ideas hit me, whether it's 2 AM or 5 AM, and I get to work. There's just not enough hours in the day to get it all done otherwise.
How many hours of sleep do you usually get in a night now, compared to before you started working on the memorial?

Well, let's see... before all this started, I was pretty regular. You know, lights out by ten, maybe ten-thirty if my wife and I were watching something good on the television, and I'd be up by six or six-thirty to get out to the garden or meet the guys for our walk. So that's what, about eight hours? Give or take. A solid eight hours. I've always been a good sleeper, never really had trouble drifting off. 

But now? Gosh, I don't even know how to count it. Like I said, I'm up and down so much. I might lay down at eleven, but then I'm back up at midnight because I remembered I need to call his old buddy Frank in Ohio, and I have to write a note so I don't forget to call him first thing. And then I'm up for an hour looking through old address books trying to find Frank's number, because I know I wrote it down in this little blue leather book I had back in '85, but I can't find the book. So then I'm tearing through the desk drawers, and before I know it, it's two in the morning. 

Then I might doze for a bit in the recliner, maybe an hour or two? But then the sun starts coming up, or I hear the paperboy, and I'm wide awake again, ready to go. I just have to get started on the displays, you know? So, if you add it all up, maybe I'm getting... I don't know, three hours? Four on a good night? But it's all broken up into these little chunks. It's hard to really put a number on it when you're not just sleeping straight through like a normal person. But like I said, I feel fine! I don't feel tired at all, which is the crazy part. You'd think I'd be exhausted, but I'm just running on all cylinders.
Have you noticed your mood being unusually high, irritable, or excited during this time, not just being busy or energetic?

Excited? Well... I guess you could say that. It’s more than just having energy, it’s like... I feel completely lit up inside, you know? Just absolutely full of purpose. I was actually down at the senior center the other day—I haven't been doing my walking group, like I said, but I went down there to talk to them about setting up one of the displays in their main hall. Because I realized, this memorial isn't just for me or my wife. Once this is all put together, the whole town is finally going to understand our family. They’re going to see what my brother was really made of, all the things he accomplished that nobody gave him credit for. It just feels incredible to be the one bringing all that to light. It's like a calling, really. 

But, on the other hand... irritable. Yeah, my wife would probably jump right out of her chair and shout 'yes' if she heard you ask that. I admit, I have been... well, snapping at her. And it's not just her, either. Like when I was at the senior center, Brenda at the front desk started hemming and hawing, asking all these ridiculous questions about how much space the display would take up, and if it would block the hallway to the bingo room, and I just... I lost my temper. I snapped right at her. 

It's the same with my wife when she comes in bothering me about the tomatoes while I'm right in the middle of cross-referencing his old letters. I mean, one minute I'm feeling on top of the world, so clear-headed and driven, and the next minute I'm biting somebody's head off. But you have to understand, they just keep slowing me down! If they wouldn't question the display or try to interrupt what I'm doing, I wouldn't get so testy. It’s just that I have this vision, and nobody else seems to grasp how important it is to just let me work.
Can you recall if there has been a period of at least a week where your mood was consistently high, overly excited, or irritable to the point that it was noticeably different from your usual self?

A week? Oh, doctor, it's been a lot longer than a week. This whole thing... this energy, this feeling of being so completely dialed in, and yes, the snapping at people... it’s been going on for about two months now. Exactly two months, give or take a few days. 

It all started right after my brother passed away. We had the funeral, and it was nice, you know, standard affair, lots of casseroles and people saying they're sorry for your loss, but it just felt so... inadequate. Like, is that it? Just a few hymns and some potato salad? That's when it hit me that I needed to do something bigger. I had to build this tribute, this memorial, so people would really understand him. 

And from the moment I made that decision, it was like a switch flipped. Boom. Suddenly, I’m up at all hours, I’ve got all these ideas flooding in, and I just feel this incredible, buzzing drive to get it all done. So, it hasn't just been a week. It’s been weeks and weeks of this. Two straight months of just... running hot, I guess you could say. My wife keeps saying, 'You need to slow down, you've been like this for weeks,' but she doesn't get that I can't just turn it off. I've been riding this wave since the day of the funeral, and I have to see it through.
